english.html: be done, and there was heard by the said Judge of Rieux.

On this subject I have sometimes seen it called into doubt, to see whether a man who is going to die can be heard as a witness, or otherwise examined by a Judge: seeing that in this kind of hearings memory and recollection are singularly required <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, which cannot well fall to one who, feeling the last breaths of his life draw near, and overcome by the hideous fright and horrible apprehension of death, is agitated and tormented in a thousand and a thousand ways <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>.

notes.gloss: The paragraph on the frailty of the dying testator; cited again at {n}. The transcribers could not settle whether the print's double s is ſſ or ß; the word is the same.

english.html: In a thousand forms of death one single death wearies the wretched (Mille modis lethi miseros mors una fatigat) c.

notes.gloss: Mille modis leti miseros mors una fatigat — by a thousand kinds of death one death wearies the wretched.

english.html: Witness our Redeemer Jesus Christ, who, foretasting the sharpness and bitterness of his dolorous passion, was sorrowful at it even unto death d, nay even to the point of grieving, and almost complaining, of God his father, saying, Heli, Heli, lama sabathani? My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me e? Nevertheless the contrary opinion is, with great reason, practised and received by all. For if he who is at the extremity of life can dispose of his goods by testament, sale, gift, and any other kind of disposition whatsoever, whether between the living or by reason of death f (in which, however, the integrity of a man's sense and understanding is greatly required g) — nay even, says the Emperor, though the dying man, crushed by sickness, were half dead and stammered with his tongue, provided that otherwise his conceptions and wishes be understood h — why is it that for the same reasons (where the case shall require it) the dying man cannot be heard and bear witness i? True it is that in this I desire the Judge, or Commissioner, who proceeds to the hearing to be prudent, wise, discreet and well advised, not to make the interrogations confused, long or prolix, but the clearest and briefest he can, comprising in few words the whole substance of the business k; inasmuch as, as has been said above, the spirit of him who feels near at hand the tearing asunder and separation of body and soul

notes.original: S. Matth. chap. xxvj. S. Marc c. xiiij.
notes.gloss: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem — my soul is sorrowful even unto death, at Gethsemane.
Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? The transcribers' first reading of the word is defective ([?]ſabathani); the alternative, aſabathani, is Coras's lama sabathani with the a carried to the second word.

notes.citation: Digest 32.39.1 (De legatis et fideicommissis III, l. Pamphilo, § Proposi[tum]); Bartolus (Bartole) on Digest 28.1 (Qui testamenta facere possunt), l. Heredes palam (D. 28.1.21, Ulpian), § Uno contextu (§ 3)
notes.original: l. Pamphylo P. propoſi. D. de leg. iij. Bar. l. hære. P. vno cont. D. de te.
notes.gloss: A testament must be made uno contextu, in one continuous act; Bartolus on the dying testator.

notes.citation: Digest 28.1 (Qui testamenta facere possunt), l. 2 (D. 28.1.2, Labeo)
notes.gloss: In eo qui testatur eius temporis, quo testamentum facit, integritas mentis, non corporis sanitas exigenda est — in a testator, soundness of mind, not health of body, is required at the time he makes the will. Coras's "integrity of a man's sense and understanding".

notes.original: l. quoniam indignum. C. de teſta.
notes.gloss: The emperor's law allowing the will of a testator who, though failing, can still make his wishes understood — Coras's "half dead and stammering".

notes.citation: Digest 28.1.26 (Qui testamenta facere possunt, l. Cum lege)
notes.original: l. cũ lege D. de teſta.

notes.citation: Baldus (Balde) on the Libri feudorum, De pace Constantiae (the Peace of Constance, appended to the feudal law), c. 1, § Vasall[us] (locus not verified)
notes.original: Balde au c. j. P. vaſſal. de pact. conſtant aux feudes.
notes.gloss: The print's de pact. conſtant is de pace Constantiae.

de Rieux.
Sur ce propos i'ay veu quelquesfois reuoquer en dou
te, pour voir ſi vn homme, qui ſ'en va mourir, peut eſtre
ouy comme teſmoin, ou autrement enquis par vn Iu-
ge: attendu qu'en telle maniere d'auditiõs eſt ſingulie-
rement deſiree, la memoire & ſouuenance {a}. Laquelle
ne peut bonnement eſchoir en celuy, qui ſentant appro
cher les derniers ſouſprirs de ſa vie, & ſurmonté de l'hi
deuſe frayeur, & horrible apprehenſion de la mort, eſt
agité & tormenté en mille & mille ſortes {b}.
Mille modus lethi, miſeros, mors vna fatigat {c}.
Teſmoin noſtre Redempteur Ieſus Chriſt, lequel pre
ſentant l'aigreur & l'amertume de ſa douloureuſe paſ-
ſion, en fut contriſté iuſqu'à la mort {d}. voire iuſqu'à ſe
douloir & preſque plaindre de Dieu ſon pere, diſant,
Heli, Heli, lam aſabathani? Mon Dieu, mon Dieu, pour-
quoy m'as tu delaiſſé {e}? Toutesfois, la cõtraire opinion
eſt à grande raiſon pratiquee de tous, & receuë. Car ſi
celuy qui eſt en extremité de vie, peut diſpoſer de ſes
biens par teſtament, vente, donnaiſon, & quelconque
autre eſpece de diſpoſition, ſoit entre vifs, ou à cauſe de
mort {f}. (eſquelles pourtãt, l'integrité du ſens, & de l'en
tendement de l'homme eſt grandement requiſe {g}) voi-
re encor, dit l'Empereur, que le moribunde accablé de
maladie, fuſt demy mort, & begueyaſt de ſa langue,
pourueu que d'ailleurs ſes conceptions & volontez
ſoyent entendues {h}. Pourquoy eſt-ce que par meſmes
raiſons (où le cas le requerra) le moribunde ne pourra
eſtre ouy, & porter teſmoignage {i}? Vray eſt qu'en cela
ie deſire le Iuge, ou Commiſſaire, qui procede à l'audi-
tion, eſtre prudent, ſage, diſcret, & bien aduiſé, de ne
faire les interrogatoires confus, longs, ni prolixes:
mais les plus clairs, & briefs qu'il pourra: comprenant
en peu de paroles toute la ſubſtãce du negoce {k}. partãt
que cõme deſſus a eſté dit, l'eſprit de celuy qui ſent pro
chaine la diuulſion, & ſeparation du corps & de l'ame
